jst_01.scenario_text: the clouds had strings attached to them which hang down to earth
anchors: If clouds had strings, pilots would avoid tangled sky corridors.
If clouds had strings, farmers could pull rain clouds toward dry fields.
If clouds had strings, children might climb or swing from low clouds.
If clouds had strings, cities would regulate anchors tied to buildings.
If clouds had strings, storms could drag objects across the ground.
If clouds had strings, cloud weaving and sky tourism could emerge.

jst_02.scenario_text: for some reason, all we could see of people would be their feet
anchors: If only feet were visible, shoes would become the main identity signal.
If only feet were visible, sidewalks would need safer foot-level signs.
If only feet were visible, people would recognize friends by gait and footwear.
If only feet were visible, fashion and advertising would move toward socks.
If only feet were visible, crowds would trip more often at crossings.
If only feet were visible, social greetings would shift to foot gestures.

jst_03.scenario_text: every suitcase would quietly follow its owner everywhere like a loyal pet
anchors: If suitcases followed owners, airport queues would reorganize around moving luggage.
If suitcases followed owners, thieves could be tracked by stolen bags.
If suitcases followed owners, sidewalks would need lanes for trailing baggage.
If suitcases followed owners, hotels would offer suitcase parking areas.
If suitcases followed owners, privacy rules would cover luggage location data.
If suitcases followed owners, travel brands would sell trained bag behaviors.

jst_04.scenario_text: every ladder grew one new rung each time someone climbed it
anchors: If ladders grew when climbed, buildings could be reached without new equipment.
If ladders grew when climbed, workers would need height limits for safety.
If ladders grew when climbed, children might turn ladders into climbing games.
If ladders grew when climbed, rescue teams could reach roofs faster.
If ladders grew when climbed, abandoned ladders could block streets or rooms.
If ladders grew when climbed, construction rules would treat them as expanding structures.

jst_05.scenario_text: every lost wallet slowly crawled back to its owner on its own
anchors: If wallets crawled home, lost-and-found desks would become less important.
If wallets crawled home, pickpockets would be easier to identify.
If wallets crawled home, streets would have tiny lanes for returning wallets.
If wallets crawled home, payment companies would advertise self-returning security.
If wallets crawled home, police could follow wallets to fraud victims.
If wallets crawled home, people might intentionally send cash by wallet.

jst_06.scenario_text: every door whispered what happened the last time it opened
anchors: If doors whispered memories, privacy around rooms would become fragile.
If doors whispered memories, police could use doors as witnesses.
If doors whispered memories, landlords would inspect apartments by listening.
If doors whispered memories, people would oil hinges to hide secrets.
If doors whispered memories, theaters could use doors as storytellers.
If doors whispered memories, quiet buildings would require soundproof entrances.

jst_07.scenario_text: every book floated a few centimeters above any table
anchors: If books floated above tables, libraries would redesign shelves and desks.
If books floated above tables, students could slide notes underneath.
If books floated above tables, spills would damage fewer pages.
If books floated above tables, floating stacks could block sight lines.
If books floated above tables, publishers might build hovering displays.
If books floated above tables, magnets and clips would keep pages steady.

jst_08.scenario_text: people's shadows changed color with their mood
anchors: If shadows showed mood, emotions would become visible in public.
If shadows showed mood, doctors could screen stress by shadow color.
If shadows showed mood, workplaces might misuse emotional surveillance.
If shadows showed mood, fashion would include mood-matching lighting.
If shadows showed mood, actors could perform with colored shadow cues.
If shadows showed mood, people would carry lamps to hide feelings.

jst_09.scenario_text: rain fell upward from puddles into clouds every afternoon
anchors: If rain rose from puddles, streets would dry in sudden upward sprays.
If rain rose from puddles, umbrellas would protect faces from below.
If rain rose from puddles, cities would redesign drains and gutters.
If rain rose from puddles, clouds could be rebuilt from ground water.
If rain rose from puddles, cyclists would avoid afternoon water jets.
If rain rose from puddles, farmers would time irrigation around upward rain.

jst_10.scenario_text: mirrors showed reflections from ten minutes ago
anchors: If mirrors lagged ten minutes, people could review recent actions.
If mirrors lagged ten minutes, security mirrors would become short replay screens.
If mirrors lagged ten minutes, grooming would become harder and slower.
If mirrors lagged ten minutes, performers could study their last rehearsal move.
If mirrors lagged ten minutes, witnesses could check what happened nearby.
If mirrors lagged ten minutes, privacy rules would cover delayed reflections.

anchors: If traffic lights sang, drivers would learn melodies for stop and go.
If traffic lights sang, cities would regulate intersection noise.
If traffic lights sang, blind pedestrians could use musical crossing cues.
If traffic lights sang, traffic jams might become noisy public concerts.
If traffic lights sang, advertising jingles could invade road signals.
If traffic lights sang, emergency routes would use special harmonies.

jst_12.scenario_text: every road stretched longer during rush hour
anchors: If roads stretched at rush hour, commutes would become unpredictable.
If roads stretched at rush hour, maps would need time-changing distances.
If roads stretched at rush hour, emergency vehicles would need priority lanes.
If roads stretched at rush hour, businesses would stagger work schedules.
If roads stretched at rush hour, bridges and pipes would need flexible joints.
If roads stretched at rush hour, cyclists might choose paths before expansion.
